title: A Tribute to Australian Senator Derryn Hinch: A Courageous Voice for Tibet and Justice - Tibet Post International
content:
Dharamshala — Australian Senator Derryn Hinch will be remembered not only as one of Australia's most fearless investigative journalists and broadcasters, but also as a parliamentarian who demonstrated the courage to speak publicly on behalf of oppressed peoples.
Throughout his distinguished career, he became widely known as the "Human Headline" for his unwavering commitment to exposing injustice, defending victims, and holding those in positions of power to account.
Australian Senator and media personality Derryn Hinch passed away peacefully in his sleep at his home in Melbourne on 10 July 2026, at the age of 82. His death marked the end of an extraordinary public life spanning more than six decades in journalism, broadcasting, and politics. Known as the “Human Headline”, Hinch was remembered for his distinctive voice, fearless advocacy, and determination to speak on issues he believed required public attention.
Among the many causes that Senator Hinch supported during his time in public life was the cause of Tibet. As leader of an Australian parliamentary delegation that visited Dharamshala, India, from 20 to 23 November 2017, he witnessed first-hand the resilience, dignity, and determination of the Tibetan people living in exile. The delegation also included the Hon. Kevin Andrews MP, Senator Kimberley Kitching, and Meryl Swanson MP, reflecting bipartisan Australian parliamentary engagement with the Tibetan issue.
During the visit, Senator Hinch met His Holiness the Dalai Lama and senior representatives of the Central Tibetan Administration. He also visited Tibetan educational and cultural institutions, gaining a deeper understanding of the challenges faced by Tibetans both inside Tibet and in exile.
Speaking at a press conference in Dharamshala, Senator Hinch expressed admiration for the Tibetan people's steadfast commitment to preserving their identity despite decades of hardship. Referring to China's demographic policies in Tibet, he remarked that attempts to overwhelm the Tibetan population had failed because the Tibetan people had refused to surrender their identity, culture, and hope. He praised their resilience and expressed confidence that their determination and commitment to peaceful dialogue would continue to sustain their struggle.
Senator Derryn Hinch expressed his admiration for the resilience and determination of the people of Tibet. Reflecting on China's policies in Tibet, he remarked, "The Chinese... have this different version of 'populate or perish'... through the Han and the other people who would populate Tibet in the hope that you will perish—and you aren't perishing." He praised the Tibetan people's strength and commitment to peaceful dialogue, adding, "We've seen signs here, your background, your backbone and your passion will see you through the Middle Way." Senator Hinch also observed that many democratic nations were becoming more willing to engage openly with the Tibet issue, stating, "You'll find, going back a few years Western nations were sometimes worried that if we meet with the Dalai Lama, will that affect our economic ties with China. I think those days are over."
Senator Hinch also observed that international attitudes towards Tibet were evolving. He noted that many democratic nations had previously been reluctant to engage openly with His Holiness the Dalai Lama for fear of jeopardising economic relations with China. In his view, however, those concerns were beginning to diminish as governments increasingly recognised the importance of defending universal values, including human rights, freedom, and justice.
The parliamentary delegation collectively called for continued international attention to the situation in Tibet. Members urged that the issue should not be forgotten and stressed the importance of maintaining peaceful international pressure to achieve a just and lasting resolution through dialogue. Their visit demonstrated that support for Tibet transcended political party affiliations and reflected shared democratic values within Australia's Parliament.
For Tibetans around the world, Senator Hinch's willingness to visit the Tibetan exile community, listen to their experiences, and speak publicly about their aspirations represented an important act of solidarity. His engagement helped bring greater visibility to a cause that has often struggled to receive sustained international attention.
Although Senator Derryn Hinch is widely remembered for his fearless journalism, advocacy for victims' rights, and distinguished parliamentary service, his support for Tibet also deserves recognition. He showed that principled leadership requires the courage to speak for those whose voices are too often ignored.
His legacy reminds us that freedom, justice, human dignity, and compassion remain universal values worthy of defence. The Tibetan people, together with many supporters of human rights around the world, will remember Senator Derryn Hinch with gratitude and respect for standing beside them during an important chapter in their modern history.
